proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 1927 article gives Malayalam kūnuka to stoop, be crookbacked; kūn a humpback; kūnal, kūntal bending; kūnan humpbacked; fem. kūni, kūnicci; kuni semicircle, curve; kuniyuka to bow, stoop, bend; kunikka to make a curve, cause to stand stooping.. The Malayalam survey form kuniy “bend” is proposed within this article family.

proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 2456 article gives Malayalam cāyka to incline, lean to one side, rest or lie on, settle down, disappear; cāyal, cāccal bending sideways as a falling tree, side, inclination; cāykka to lean against, bend, put one on the other, lower, level the ground by beating, lie down to sleep;…. The Malayalam survey form cāy “bend” is proposed within this article family.

proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 2360 article gives Malayalam cariyuka to slide, slip, roll down, lean, bend; carikka to bend, make to lean sidewards, lower a vessel, pour; carippikka to cause to lean; cariccal a low shed, sideroom; carivu, caru inclination, slope, bending; carkuka to glide, slide; arikka to creep…. The Malayalam survey form cariy “bend” is proposed within this article family.

proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 1124 article gives Malayalam kaṭikka to bite, chew, smart, pain, cheat; kaṭiyuka to be pained, broken; kaṭi a bite, biting; a cheat.. The Malayalam survey form kaḍikky “bite” is proposed within this article family. Lindgren assigns the corresponding Tamil reflex to the same source cognate set.
